question: What is the main job of sensory input in our nervous system?

options.A: Sending commands directly to the skeletal muscles
options.B: Detecting changes inside and outside the body
options.C: Producing hormones to regulate blood pressure
options.D: Processing complex thoughts in the spinal cord

explanation: Think of sensory input as your body's early warning system. Receptors pick up information from both your external environment and your insides so you can react! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T6#GNS211_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why do nurses regularly monitor a child's growth?

options.A: To calculate exact adult height and weight
options.B: To diagnose specific genetic disorders instantly
options.C: To catch health and nutritional problems early
options.D: To replace routine medical checkups entirely

explanation: You've got this! Growth monitoring helps us spot tiny changes or downward trends early on, long before a child gets seriously ill. It's a quick win for preventive care! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T005#GNS227_U2_T005_h1)

question: What is the definitive treatment when acute foetal distress does not respond to conservative resuscitation?

options.A: Strict bed rest for the mother
options.B: Administration of oral antibiotics
options.C: Monitoring for another two hours
options.D: Emergency delivery of the foetus

explanation: If the baby remains starved of oxygen despite nursing interventions, the only way to save it is to deliver the baby promptly. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h6)

question: A community health nurse is teaching villagers how Ebola spreads. Which practice should she warn against the most?

options.A: Drinking boiled water from a community well during dry seasons
options.B: Eating well-cooked pork from certified local livestock farms
options.C: Washing the body of a relative who died from suspected Ebola
options.D: Sharing eating utensils with a family member who has malaria

explanation: Well done! The viral load is super high in someone who just passed away, making traditional burial touching very risky. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h2)

question: Why do health workers treat gender-based violence as a major public health emergency?

options.A: It only affects women living in rural environments
options.B: It primarily places financial strain on hospital pharmacies
options.C: It causes widespread physical and psychological harm across communities
options.D: It is classified as a rare infectious disease outbreak

explanation: You got it! Because it hurts so many people physically and emotionally, healthcare systems treat it as a top priority to keep communities safe. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T23#GNS225_U5_T23_h1)

question: Why do nurses need to understand health care costs?

options.A: To diagnose complex financial diseases in the community
options.B: To calculate daily profits for the hospital pharmacy
options.C: To help patients navigate financial strain and advocate for them
options.D: To replace hospital accountants during budget reviews

explanation: You will often see how money worries affect your patients. Knowing about healthcare costs helps you support and speak up for them when they face tough financial choices. [learn more](GST322_U2_T1#GST322_U2_T1_h1)

question: What is the main function of a computerized staffing system?

options.A: To calculate the exact financial salary of every hospital worker
options.B: To track the expiration dates of intravenous fluids in the pharmacy
options.C: To monitor patient vital signs remotely from a central nursing station
options.D: To generate balanced work schedules based on patient needs and staff skills

explanation: Staffing software matches patient census data and nurse competencies to create safe shift rosters. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h4)

question: Why is it important for clinical nurses to be involved when designing new health software?

options.A: To write the computer programming code and fix hardware bugs
options.B: To replace hospital administrators during board meetings
options.C: To ensure the technology actually matches real-world bedside workflows
options.D: To market the software to other hospitals for profit

explanation: Involving nurses ensures that digital systems are practical and helpful in actual clinical practice rather than creating unnecessary obstacles. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h6)

question: As a Nigerian nurse, what is a key part of your role when it comes to community nutrition?

options.A: Formulating industrial food additives in factories
options.B: Replacing all traditional farming with foreign grains
options.C: Educating communities and managing cases of malnutrition
options.D: Exporting local cash crops to international markets

explanation: That's right! Nurses are frontline educators. We spot nutritional gaps in our clinics and teach mothers the best ways to feed their families. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T002#GNS227_U1_T002_h6)

question: What makes an intragroup conflict unique among nurses on the same ward?

options.A: It happens among members of the exact same team.
options.B: It arises strictly from a lack of hospital medical equipment.
options.C: It only occurs between nurses and hospital administrators.
options.D: It involves a nurse arguing with a patient's family member.

explanation: Intragroup conflict happens right within a single, close-knit team—like coworkers on your own shift disagreeing on how to run things. [learn more](GST321_U5_T1#GST321_U5_T1_h3)

question: You are plotting patient age on the X-axis and length of stay on the Y-axis. After drawing your blank axes, what is next?

options.A: Erase the axis labels to make the chart look cleaner
options.B: Calculate the percentage of patients over the age of sixty
options.C: Draw a straight line connecting every single dot in order
options.D: Scale the axes with equal intervals to fit the data values

explanation: Before plotting dots, you need to set up your numbers evenly along the axes so your graph is accurate and easy to read. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T12#GNS217_U4_T12_h4)

question: Why can spotting an adverse drug reaction sometimes be tricky for a nurse on the ward?

options.A: Patients refuse to talk about how they feel after taking drugs.
options.B: The symptoms often look like common illnesses or the original disease.
options.C: Laboratory tests always show normal values during a drug reaction.
options.D: ADRs only occur when the patient is discharged from the hospital.

explanation: It's easy to miss because signs like nausea, dizziness, or headache can easily be mistaken for the patient's actual sickness getting worse. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T8#GNS125_U5_T8_h3)

question: What is a major feature that sets connective tissue apart from epithelial tissue?

options.A: Its cells are always tightly packed together without space
options.B: It never has any blood supply running through it
options.C: It contains a large amount of extracellular matrix
options.D: It is found exclusively on the outer surface of the skin

explanation: Unlike epithelial cells which pack tightly together, connective tissue cells are spread out in a rich matrix of fibers and ground substance. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h4)

question: Why is it so important to find the root cause of a gap found during an audit?

options.A: To justify closing down the nursing department permanently
options.B: To make sure every single nurse on duty receives a formal warning
options.C: So the corrective action actually fixes the real underlying problem
options.D: To prove that the hospital administration has zero funds left

explanation: You nailed it! Finding the root cause ensures we fix the actual issue—whether it's a lack of training or a shortage of supplies—rather than just guessing. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h6)

question: What is one of the biggest challenges nurses face when taking skinfold measurements?

options.A: Variations in technique between nurses can lead to inconsistent results
options.B: It is impossible to perform on patients who are conscious
options.C: The test causes permanent bruising at the anatomical site
options.D: The equipment requires a continuous electrical power source

explanation: You got it! Skinfold testing takes practice. If two different nurses pinch slightly different spots or angles, they might get different readings. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T003#GNS227_U5_T003_h6)

question: Which metabolic process involves building complex body tissues from simpler substances?

options.A: Excretion
options.B: Catabolism
options.C: Anabolism
options.D: Digestion

explanation: Think of 'Anabolism' as adding blocks to build things up—like turning simple amino acids into strong muscles. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T001#GNS227_U1_T001_h6)

question: You pick up a sterile tray and notice the outer wrap is damp. What should you do?

options.A: Dry the outer packaging with a clean paper towel and use it immediately
options.B: Open the pack and quickly wipe down the interior instruments with alcohol
options.C: Reject the tray and obtain a new one because moisture causes contamination
options.D: Place the pack back into the warming cabinet until the moisture evaporates

explanation: Wet packs are a no-go! Moisture lets germs soak straight through the paper wrap, contaminating the instruments inside. [learn more](GST114_U2_T11#GST114_U2_T11_h7)

question: What is the main operational strategy used for disease surveillance in Nigerian health facilities?

options.A: Federal Hospital Statistical Monitoring
options.B: National Emergency Health Record System
options.C: Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response
options.D: Community Primary Care Diagnostic Network

explanation: The IDSR strategy is the standardized framework used across Nigerian health facilities to detect and report priority diseases. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h4)

question: Why must nurses keep reassessing patients who have already been sorted into a triage category?

options.A: Rescue teams need to change patient names frequently
options.B: Color tags often fall off in wet weather conditions
options.C: Hospital admission clerks require updated paperwork every hour
options.D: A patient's condition can rapidly deteriorate over time

explanation: Exactly! Injuries can hide beneath the surface, meaning a patient who looks stable now could crash and need urgent help a few minutes later. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T3#GNS315_U5_T3_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of a post-incident debriefing or 'hot wash' session?

options.A: To review performance, identify communication failures, and improve future responses
options.B: To audit employee payroll and overtime hours for budget approval
options.C: To assign personal blame and punishment to staff members who made mistakes
options.D: To celebrate the end of the shift with recreational activities

explanation: Debriefs aren't about pointing fingers; they're safe spaces to figure out what went well and what can be fixed for next time. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T1#GNS315_U5_T1_h7)

question: An adult patient is overwhelmed by job loss and financial stress. Which nursing intervention best helps build resilience?

options.A: Teaching structured problem-solving and healthy emotional coping methods
options.B: Recommending that the patient avoid all future employment opportunities
options.C: Encouraging the patient to isolate until all financial problems are solved
options.D: Telling the patient to ignore the stress because things always work out

explanation: Teaching actionable problem-solving and healthy coping empowers patients to face crises constructively and builds long-term resilience. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT an essential supply needed for comprehensive PAC services?

options.A: Contraceptive commodities
options.B: Chemotherapy infusion pumps
options.C: Uterotonic medications
options.D: Infection prevention PPE

explanation: You'll find chemotherapy pumps in cancer care wards, not in standard Post-Abortion Care clinics! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h3)

question: If a study shows a significant link between long shifts and nurse burnout, what is the best takeaway for hospital managers?

options.A: Increase shift lengths further to test the null hypothesis again
options.B: Dismiss the finding because statistical tests never apply to real hospitals
options.C: Review and adjust staff shift scheduling policies to reduce burnout
options.D: Switch all patient data collection methods to continuous numerical scales

explanation: Spot on! Research is meant to guide practical changes that improve staff well-being and patient safety in our hospitals. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T13#GNS217_U4_T13_h7)

question: When does the debriefing session take place in the simulation learning cycle?

options.A: Before the students even read their patient charts
options.B: Immediately after the simulation scenario finishes
options.C: Only when a student fails a practical examination
options.D: Several weeks after the clinical rotation is finished

explanation: Debriefing happens right after the scenario while the events and emotions are still fresh in the students' minds. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T8#GNS212_U4_T8_h5)

question: Which action shows a wonderful balance of efficiency, effectiveness, and equity in a local health program?

options.A: Saving money by refusing to treat patients who cannot pay cash on arrival
options.B: Using low-cost, proven malaria treatments distributed freely to pregnant women in remote villages
options.C: Employing double the required staff for every shift to ensure nobody feels rushed
options.D: Purchasing expensive imported machines that only wealthy patients in the capital can afford

explanation: Brilliant! This uses funds wisely (efficiency), cures malaria reliably (effectiveness), and reaches mothers who need it most for free (equity). [learn more](GST322_U4_T6#GST322_U4_T6_h7)

question: A nurse is preparing a flexible endoscope that touches mucous membranes. What level of germ control does this need?

options.A: Standard mechanical cleaning
options.B: Low-level disinfection
options.C: Routine surface wiping
options.D: High-level disinfection

explanation: Right on! Anything touching mucous membranes is 'semi-critical' and needs high-level disinfection to knock out almost all pathogens, keeping our patients safe. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which group of vitamins needs dietary fat to be properly absorbed by the body?

options.A: Water-soluble B-complex vitamins
options.B: Trace mineral cofactors
options.C: Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K)
options.D: Ascorbic acid and related compounds

explanation: Correct! Vitamins A, D, E, and K dissolve in fats, so you need some dietary fat to absorb them into your bloodstream. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T006#GNS227_U6_T006_h6)

question: An 85-year-old retired civil servant comes to the clinic with joint pain and feeling very lonely. Which government program can help with both issues?

options.A: Giving them a heavy-duty vehicle driving license
options.B: Enrolling them in mandatory military training
options.C: Sending them to a full-time industrial workshop
options.D: Geriatric care integration and social protection programs

explanation: Great choice! Specialized geriatric care treats their physical aches, while social programs step in to beat loneliness and build community connection. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T26#GNS225_U5_T26_h4)

question: How do neuroglial cells differ from neurons?

options.A: Neurons provide physical support rather than signaling.
options.B: Glial cells are incapable of cell division.
options.C: Neurons are much smaller than neuroglial cells.
options.D: Glial cells do not transmit nerve impulses.

explanation: Glial cells are the supportive helpers and cheerleaders for neurons, but they don't carry the electrical signals themselves. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h7)

question: How does educating a patient help reduce inappropriate drug use?

options.A: It prevents them from ever visiting a hospital clinic again
options.B: It helps them understand why they do not need certain medicines
options.C: It forces pharmaceutical companies to lower medication prices
options.D: It gives them the legal right to prescribe drugs to neighbors

explanation: When patients understand the risks of unnecessary drugs, they are less likely to demand them from clinicians. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h6)

question: Which of these is the main reproductive organ in females?

options.A: Uterus
options.B: Fallopian tube
options.C: Ovary
options.D: Vagina

explanation: Spot on! The ovaries are the primary organs because they make the eggs and female hormones. The rest are helper structures. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T3#GNS121_U5_T3_h1)

question: As a nurse, what is a key action when helping a patient deal with the emotional side of sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Discouraging partner involvement in therapy
options.B: Prescribing anti-anxiety medications directly
options.C: Validating feelings and offering referrals
options.D: Diagnosing deep psychiatric disorders

explanation: Brilliant! Creating a safe, judgment-free space and connecting them with a trained counselor makes all the difference in their care. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T24#GNS312_U1_T24_h7)

question: What is required before a human participant can take part in a research study?

options.A: A signed agreement to work on the ward
options.B: Voluntary informed consent
options.C: Approval from hospital accountants
options.D: Payment of a research fee

explanation: Ethics first! Participants must fully understand what the study involves and willingly agree to join without any pressure. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T2#GNS217_U1_T2_h8)

question: Why do nurses take out the inner cannula to clean or replace it?

options.A: To deflate the cuff automatically
options.B: To prevent dried secretions from blocking the airway
options.C: To change the size of the outer tube
options.D: To allow the patient to drink water safely

explanation: Mucus loves to build up inside the tube! Cleaning or swapping the inner cannula keeps the airway clear so the patient can breathe easily. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T1#GNS315_U4_T1_h3)

question: Which hormone helps your kidneys save water when your body is dehydrated?

options.A: Anti-diuretic hormone
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Thyroxine
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Think of Anti-diuretic hormone (ADH) as your body's 'anti-pee' signal. It tells your kidney collecting ducts to hold onto water so you don't get dehydrated. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T1#GNS213_U4_T1_h5)

question: What happens when hospital administrators treat MBO as just a bureaucratic checklist?

options.A: Patient satisfaction increases across all departments
options.B: The hospital saves money on administrative salaries
options.C: Staff quickly lose interest and trust in the process
options.D: Nurses become expert planners overnight

explanation: When MBO lacks genuine leadership commitment and becomes mere paperwork, staff view it as a burden rather than a useful tool. [learn more](GST321_U2_T4#GST321_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why do nurses ask patients to close their eyes during a simple touch sensation check?

options.A: To stop the pupils from reacting to bright light
options.B: To help the patient relax their heart rate
options.C: To prevent visual cues from replacing or biasing touch feedback
options.D: To prevent dizziness caused by looking around the room

explanation: Smart nursing practice! Closing the eyes makes sure we are strictly testing the patient's nerves and feeling, not letting their eyes do the guessing. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T11#GNS211_U4_T11_h7)

question: What is a common result of having very restrictive abortion laws in developing countries?

options.A: Better funding and equipment for public maternity hospitals
options.B: Improved cooperation between traditional healers and doctors
options.C: The complete eradication of unintended pregnancies in society
options.D: An increase in dangerous, clandestine procedures performed by unqualified people

explanation: Correct. Making a procedure illegal doesn't stop it; it just drives desperate patients into secret, unsafe places. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h5)

question: Where is the scheduled date for a child's next vaccine dose primarily recorded for the mother to see?

options.A: On the pharmacy prescription ledger
options.B: On the child's home-based health card
options.C: In the national budget allocation report
options.D: In the local government tax receipt

explanation: The child health card stays with the caregiver and serves as the primary personal reminder for upcoming immunization dates. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h3)

question: Why does poor human waste disposal quickly lead to community illness?

options.A: It attracts large livestock that carry respiratory viruses
options.B: It lowers the nutritional value of locally grown crops
options.C: It contaminates local water sources and soil used by the community
options.D: It directly increases the air temperature and humidity in homes

explanation: Think about it like this: when waste isn't disposed of properly, germs easily wash into our daily water and soil. That's how infections spread fast in a neighborhood! [learn more](GST114_U6_T3#GST114_U6_T3_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal market problem (imperfection) in healthcare?

options.A: Adverse selection where mostly sick people join insurance plans
options.B: Patients having perfect, expert knowledge of all complex medical treatments
options.C: Information asymmetry between the doctor and the patient
options.D: Moral hazard linked to having full health insurance

explanation: Well done! Patients definitely do *not* have perfect medical knowledge. The reality that patients lack this insider knowledge is actually a major market imperfection! [learn more](GST322_U1_T3#GST322_U1_T3_h5)

question: A patient complains that their prescribed diet cuts out all their favorite cultural dishes and feels impossible. What is your best response?

options.A: Tell the patient they have no choice and must strictly obey the prescription
options.B: Work with the patient to find healthy substitutes and modify their favorite cultural meals
options.C: Ignore the complaint since food preferences do not affect health outcomes
options.D: Advise the patient to stop eating entirely until they adjust to the new menu

explanation: That's patient-centered care! Respecting their culture and tweaking their favorite meals makes it much more likely they will stick to the plan. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h6)

question: Why is it so important to keep interruptions in chest compressions to a bare minimum when using an AED?

options.A: The AED machine will shut down if compressions continue too long
options.B: Stopping compressions lowers blood flow to the brain and heart
options.C: Pausing compressions causes the AED pads to lose their sticky adhesive
options.D: Continuous motion prevents the AED from detecting breathing sounds

explanation: Every second you pause compressions, blood pressure drops and the brain loses vital oxygen. Keep your hands on the chest as much as possible! [learn more](GNS315_U4_T3#GNS315_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of an under-water seal drainage system?

options.A: To restore negative pressure in the pleural space
options.B: To measure the exact daily urine output of a patient
options.C: To pump sterile water directly into the lung tissue
options.D: To deliver high-flow oxygen straight into the chest cavity

explanation: The primary goal of chest tube drainage is to evacuate air or fluid, thereby re-establishing the normal negative pressure needed for lung expansion. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T15#GNS213_U2_T15_h1)

question: How does severe malnutrition with low blood protein (albumin) affect highly protein-bound drugs?

options.A: Kidneys flush the medication out immediately without any effect
options.B: The liver instantly destroys the drug before it reaches any target
options.C: More free drug is available in the blood, increasing toxicity risk
options.D: The drug binds tighter to tissues and never enters the bloodstream

explanation: Think of blood proteins like seats on a bus for drugs. If there aren't enough seats (albumin), more drugs float around freely in the blood, which can easily lead to an accidental overdose effect! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T10#GNS125_U5_T10_h3)

question: Which social factor is consistently proven to help young girls delay marriage and early childbearing?

options.A: Traditional community ceremonies
options.B: Living in an urban city center
options.C: Access to formal education
options.D: Employment in the agricultural sector

explanation: Education is a powerful tool! When girls stay in school, they gain knowledge, open up better life opportunities, and naturally delay marriage and childbearing. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T1#GNS216_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which of these is a factual note rather than a personal opinion?

options.A: Patient refuses medication because they are difficult
options.B: Patient states pain level is 8 out of 10
options.C: Patient is acting very annoying today
options.D: Patient seems depressed about their diagnosis

explanation: Well done! Stating exact numbers and direct quotes keeps your charting objective and free from personal bias. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h4)

question: How does expanding mandatory health insurance help solve healthcare financing problems?

options.A: It creates a reliable, pooled fund that reduces financial barriers for patients
options.B: It allows doctors to set their own salaries without government review
options.C: It forces international donors to double their annual monetary grants
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for primary healthcare centers

explanation: Brilliant! Mandatory insurance keeps a steady flow of money coming into hospitals while saving everyday people from sudden, crushing medical bills. [learn more](GST322_U5_T4#GST322_U5_T4_h8)

question: What is the key difference between process evaluation and outcome evaluation?

options.A: Process happens before planning, while outcome happens during assessment
options.B: Process is done by doctors, while outcome is done strictly by patients
options.C: Process looks at activities done, while outcome looks at the final results achieved
options.D: Process measures money spent, while outcome measures the weather

explanation: You got it! Process check-ins ask 'Did we do the activities we planned?' while outcome checks ask 'Did health actually improve?' [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h7)

question: Which type of financial control happens BEFORE an expense actually occurs?

options.A: Punitive control
options.B: Detective control
options.C: Corrective control
options.D: Preventive control

explanation: Just like prevention in nursing care, preventive controls are set up beforehand to stop mistakes or bad spending before they happen. [learn more](GST321_U1_T23#GST321_U1_T23_h3)

question: Which of the following is a key component of Primary Health Care from the Alma-Ata Declaration?

options.A: Provision of safe water and basic sanitation
options.B: Establishing private plastic surgery clinics
options.C: Building high-tech organ transplant centers
options.D: Manufacturing luxury pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Clean water and basic sanitation are absolute foundation stones for preventing diseases in any community. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which parenting style is known for being extremely strict, demanding, and low on emotional warmth?

options.A: Permissive
options.B: Authoritarian
options.C: Democratic
options.D: Authoritative

explanation: Authoritarian parenting is like a strict military commander—lots of rigid rules, but very little emotional warmth or room for discussion. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T1#GNS314_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is the main goal of qualitative research in nursing?

options.A: Calculating patient mortality rates
options.B: Understanding human experiences and meanings
options.C: Measuring exact physiological vital signs
options.D: Comparing medication dosages and outcomes

explanation: You've got this! Qualitative research is all about exploring real-life experiences, feelings, and the personal meanings people attach to health events, rather than just crunching numbers. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T5#GNS224_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which part of the brain is responsible for releasing Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH)?

options.A: The hypothalamus
options.B: The cerebral cortex
options.C: The cerebellum
options.D: The medulla oblongata

explanation: You got it! The hypothalamus acts as the master control center in the brain, pulsing out GnRH to kickstart reproductive development. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T13#GNS121_U5_T13_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical challenge faced by local emergency responders in Nigeria?

options.A: Abundant surplus of modern emergency helicopters in every local clinic
options.B: Poor inter-agency coordination during major crises
options.C: Delays in communication channels
options.D: Inadequate funding for disaster preparedness

explanation: Spot on! Local clinics usually struggle with shortages rather than having an overabundance of expensive equipment like helicopters. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T12#GNS315_U1_T12_h6)

question: What is a primary clinical responsibility of a psychiatric nurse in a CBR program?

options.A: Ordering all medical supplies directly from international factories
options.B: Managing the financial budget of the national ministry of health
options.C: Constructing physical buildings for local primary health centers
options.D: Monitoring medication compliance and watching for signs of relapse

explanation: Nurses regularly check if clients are taking their drugs correctly and observe for early behavioral changes that indicate the illness might be returning. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h3)

question: Why do some experienced healthcare staff initially resist shifting from paper charts to electronic health records?

options.A: They are legally forbidden by hospital policy from touching computer keyboards
options.B: They believe digital records make patient care completely invisible to doctors
options.C: They are comfortable with traditional paper habits and fear learning complex new software
options.D: They prefer spending extra hours manually searching through heavy filing cabinets

explanation: Change management is difficult because staff accustomed to paper workflows often feel intimidated or inconvenienced by new technology. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h5)

question: A nurse sees that the clinic's reported vaccinations are way higher than the empty vaccine vials thrown away. What should she suspect?

options.A: High community participation in outreach
options.B: Excellent storage conditions in the cold room
options.C: Proper functioning of the vaccine refrigerator
options.D: Inaccurate or inflated data recording

explanation: When the numbers on paper don't match the physical empty vials, it usually points to poor record-keeping or inflated numbers. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T75#GNS214_U1_T75_h3)

question: Why is it important to tape or strap the catheter tubing to the patient's thigh?

options.A: It prevents pulling and friction injuries inside the fragile urethral canal
options.B: It eliminates the need for daily perineal hygiene care
options.C: It speeds up the rate of urine production from the kidneys
options.D: It prevents the drainage bag from filling up too quickly

explanation: Spot on! Securing the tube stops body movements from tugging on it, protecting delicate tissues from painful friction. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T21#GNS212_U1_T21_h6)

question: What is the best nursing advice for a mum with painful, engorged breasts?

options.A: Instructing her to stop all fluid intake for the next three days
options.B: Advising her to wait twelve hours between feeds to rest the tissue
options.C: Applying ice packs to completely block the prolactin hormone

question: A community health nurse is advising local food vendors. Which safe practice should be encouraged the most?

question: What does the letter 'E' stand for in the health acronym IEC?

question: What are the main signs that tell you it's time to grab and use an AED?

question: A primary health clinic has a leaking roof and constant drug shortages. Which local committee is best positioned to address this at the facility level?

question: How do pelvic adhesions and scar tissue lead to trouble getting pregnant?

question: Why do middlemen often add to the final retail cost of food items?

question: Which pH test result tells you that the nasogastric tube is successfully resting in the stomach?

question: Why does the formal healthcare system train Traditional Birth Attendants (TBAs)?

question: Why are IV fluids given to a patient with a severe crush injury before they are freed?

question: Why might a wonder drug that wins lab awards perform poorly in a rural community?

options.A: Patients may struggle with storage requirements or fail to complete the full dosage course

question: Why do fat-soluble drugs often get absorbed right back into the bloodstream from the kidney tubules?

question: A community health nurse wants to reduce head injuries among local commercial motorcycle riders. What is the best step to take?

options.A: Fines for patients who report to the hospital injured

question: When should a nurse apply standard precautions during patient care?

question: What is the most common type of prospective observational study used in healthcare research?

explanation: Cohort studies follow groups of participants over time to observe the development of specific health outcomes. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h2)

question: What critical allergy information must you check before giving any new drug?

options.D: Reactions to household cleaning supplies

question: Which major medical breakthrough in the 1950s helped patients leave large asylums for community care?

options.A: The introduction of early psychotropic medications
options.B: The discovery of routine electroconvulsive therapy
options.C: The invention of the modern stethoscope
options.D: The creation of structured group psychotherapy

explanation: Spot on! When drugs like chlorpromazine were introduced, they helped calm severe symptoms. This meant patients could finally leave massive psychiatric asylums and receive care closer to home. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T1#GNS314_U1_T1_h2)

question: When would a nurse researcher decide to use a non-experimental design?

options.A: When ethical reasons prevent assigning patients to a harmful exposure
options.B: When proving that a specific nursing intervention directly causes a cure
options.C: When testing the exact dosage of a brand new surgical medication

question: Why are older adults more likely to experience adverse drug reactions?

options.A: Their bodies absorb medications much faster than younger people
options.B: Older skin cannot absorb pills properly
options.C: They always refuse to take prescribed doses
options.D: Age-related slowdown in kidney and liver function

question: How do descriptive statistics help nurses in everyday evidence-based practice?

question: How can a simple skin infection turn into a body-wide emergency?

question: What happens in the body when Beta-2 adrenergic receptors are stimulated?

options.C: Constriction of peripheral blood vessels

question: Why must a delivery kit with a torn or punctured wrapper be discarded or replaced?

question: Which cells in the stomach secrete hydrochloric acid?

question: Which condition features flashbacks, avoiding reminders, and being constantly on edge long after a disaster?

question: Through which bone does smell nerve fibers pass to reach the brain?

question: Why do doctors often prefer Manual Vacuum Aspiration (MVA) over sharp metal instruments for early pregnancy care?

question: What type of data is best shown using a histogram?

question: Which of these is NOT a good practice when collecting data for an explanatory study?

question: Which type of nursery is typically set up directly by a company to support its workers?

question: When auditors talk about the 'scope' of a management audit, what do they mean?

question: Which hormone surge gives the final push to release an egg from the ovary?

question: Which of these symptoms means a food handler needs to step away from work right away?

question: What should a nurse do when faced with an unclear or ambiguous prescription order?

question: What shape is the anterior fontanelle (the soft spot towards the front of a baby's head)?

question: What is the purpose of 'member checking' in a qualitative study?

question: What is it called when a drug is excreted in bile, absorbed from the gut, and returned to the bloodstream in a continuous loop?

question: Why is removing patient names and personal details (de-identifying) so important in chart review studies?

question: A home health nurse observes that a family stores leftover prescription antibiotics on a low kitchen table. What is the most appropriate action?

question: Why is it smart for you, as a student nurse, to understand local social patterns before launching a health program?

question: What is the best way for a nurse to open a conversation about grief with a newly bereaved family member?

question: What structural feature keeps the trachea open and stops it from collapsing?

question: A patient took a drug that leaves the body mainly through urine. As a nurse, how can you help speed up this process?

question: Why are human reservoirs (like people carrying a germ) harder to track than stationary things like soil?

options.B: Infected humans can move freely and spread pathogens before showing symptoms
options.C: Human carriers are completely immune to all forms of standard medical treatment

question: What is the medical term for an infection of the lower urinary tract involving the bladder?

question: What is the main job of the lower spinal cord (sacral segments) during the parasympathetic defecation reflex?

question: Which agricultural expense involves paying planting crews and harvesting staff?

question: How do feelings of disgust often shape food taboos in a society?

question: What is the main goal of doing a Root Cause Analysis (RCA)?

question: Which policy extra is especially helpful if you have to face an inquiry from the state nursing board?

question: Why is integrating basic mental health services into primary healthcare clinics an effective strategy?

question: A patient comes in with ringworm, a skin condition that loves warm and damp places. Which class of pathogen is causing this?

question: What is the term for a dangerous loop where low blood pressure weakens the heart, which then lowers blood pressure even further?

question: Which of these is a common risk for patients during a long-distance medical transport?

question: Why can unending, chronic stress eventually lead to long-term anxiety or panic?

question: How does a heavy nurse-to-patient workload negatively impact the implementation of care standards?

question: What is the main difference between monitoring and evaluating a health communication program?

options.C: Monitoring tracks daily activities, while evaluation measures long-term impact

question: What is the best way to give nutrition advice to teenage girls in a local community?

question: What is the biggest weakness of using the rational (logical) method by itself?

question: What is a big plus of having homestead gardens in rural areas?

question: What is the main job of a 'hard stop' in a computer health system?

question: Which of these is NOT a typical side effect of immune checkpoint inhibitors?

question: Which statement best captures the dimensional approach to mental health?

options.B: It ignores mild symptoms in favor of severe crises
options.C: It assigns every patient a rigid, permanent label

question: Why is a host so important in the disease transmission cycle?

question: Why is it better to call for an emergency medical assistance team early instead of waiting for a full cardiac arrest?

options.A: It reduces the cost of hospital medications.

options.C: It prevents doctors from having to do paperwork later.

question: A 24-year-old woman who used to have regular monthly periods suddenly stops menstruating for eight months. What is this called?

options.C: Delayed puberty

question: Why do vulvitis and vaginitis often happen together?

options.A: The vaginal canal produces secretions that protect the vulva from damage.

options.C: Infections always start inside the uterus first.

question: When teaching a patient about nutrition, which factor must you always keep in mind?

options.B: The specific color of the nursing uniform

options.D: The manufacturer of the IV infusion pump

question: During a Mental Status Examination, which section checks if a patient is seeing or hearing things that aren't there?

options.B: Thought content
options.C: General cognition
options.D: Motor speech

question: What is the medical word for the changing shape of a baby's skull caused by pressure during labour?

question: Why do governments keep large national strategic grain reserves?

options.C: To replace the need for local farmers to grow staple crops

question: Which question best reflects the true spirit of a Root Cause Analysis?

options.C: How many disciplinary strikes does this worker have on file?

question: Why are growth hormone and thyroid hormones so critical during infancy and childhood?

options.C: They control the immediate fight-or-flight stress reaction
options.D: They coordinate normal skeletal growth and brain maturation

question: Which of these tasks is generally NOT okay to delegate to an auxiliary nurse?

options.A: Measuring and recording routine weight on a admission scale

question: Which practice helps prevent visual eavesdropping on patient electronic health records in a busy ward?

question: Which body parts are included in the appendicular region?

question: How did later revisions of Nigeria's population policy change compared to the 1988 version?

question: What should you do if you notice a colleague accidentally contaminate a sterile setup during a procedure?

question: Which of the following is NOT permitted when managing an emergency patient who lacks capacity?

question: What is the medical term when individual cells grow larger in size?

question: What is selective reporting in research?

question: Why is the link between poor nutrition and infections called a vicious cycle?

question: Which rehab team member helps patients master everyday tasks like eating, bathing, and dressing?

question: What is the first life-saving goal when treating a patient with heavy bleeding from an abortion?

question: In a busy clinical setting, what does 'cognitive load' refer to?

question: Which of these sources is the most trusted and reliable for an academic literature review?

question: Why is learning about parasites so crucial for nurses practicing in tropical areas like Nigeria?

question: What is the main goal of using patient assistive devices in healthcare?

question: Why does IMNCI use syndromic case management instead of waiting for lab tests?

question: What should you do immediately after a drain is successfully pulled out from a surgical wound?

question: During the dry season, which water source is most risky for catching Guinea worm?

question: Why is it so important to support family members emotionally during a patient's final days?

question: What is a common barrier that nurses frequently encounter in community mental health care?

question: What do we mean when we say a bacterium has innate resistance?

question: What usually happens in a ward that is poorly organized?

question: Which of these is a direct medical cost in patient care?

question: Which drug route is usually used when you cannot find an emergency IV line?

question: Severe sleep deprivation affects a nurse's reaction time and judgment similarly to which of the following?

question: Which of these is most likely to cause daily, grinding stress that damages family relationships?

question: A patient on continuous tube feeding has a red, sore spot right on the edge of their nostril. What should you do?

question: Why does a pregnant woman's body become more sensitive to carbon dioxide?

question: When is it necessary to pop on a pair of clean gloves during an exam?

question: A nurse plans to visit a client living in a remote area with a history of unpredictable aggression. What is the safest action?

question: How do monitoring devices improve nursing documentation?

question: What does a black, tarry stool sample usually tell you about your patient?

question: How is monitoring different from evaluation in a community health project?

options.D: Monitoring focuses only on money, while evaluation focuses only on weather

question: Why is it important for nurses to know that lymph drainage differs between the upper and lower reproductive organs?

options.A: It determines the specific pathway by which infections and cancer cells spread
options.B: It prevents accidental rupture of major arteries during routine examinations
options.C: It dictates the exact rate of intravenous fluid absorption in pelvic tissues
options.D: It controls the hormonal feedback loops regulating monthly ovulation cycles

explanation: You got it! Knowing where lymph drains helps us track how infections travel and how diseases like cancer might spread in the pelvis. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T3#GNS121_U5_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary clinical advantage of active immunity over passive immunity?

options.A: Active immunity does not require exposure to any antigens
options.B: Active immunity can be easily transferred through blood transfusions
options.C: Active immunity lasts much longer due to immunological memory
options.D: Active immunity provides immediate protection within minutes

explanation: When the body creates its own antibodies and memory cells during active immunity, it remembers the germ and protects against future exposures for years. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h2)

question: Why are people with long-term leg swelling at higher risk for skin infections like cellulitis?

options.A: Swollen legs attract insects that transmit bacterial infections.
options.B: Increased blood flow carries too many white blood cells to the skin.
options.C: Fluid buildup inside the tissues directly manufactures harmful bacteria.
options.D: Stretched, fragile skin easily develops cracks that let bacteria enter.

explanation: Exactly! When skin is constantly stretched out by fluid, it gets dry, thin, and fragile. Tiny cracks form easily, giving bacteria an easy doorway in. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T14#GNS123_U3_T14_h6)

question: When is the right time to start transmission-based precautions for a patient?

options.A: At the first sign of symptoms or upon suspicion of infection
options.B: After public health officers visit the ward
options.C: When the patient requests a private hospital room
options.D: Only after laboratory confirmation is fully finalized

explanation: Spot on! Waiting for lab results takes time, and germs don't wait. As soon as you suspect an infection, start precautions right away to keep everyone safe. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h1)

question: In pharmacy inventory management, what does the rule 'FIFO' stand for?

options.A: Free Inspection For Orders
options.B: Find It, Fix It Out
options.C: Fastest Item Found Online
options.D: First-In, First-Out

explanation: Easy to remember: First-In, First-Out (FIFO) means the drugs that arrived first should be the ones dispensed first! [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h4)

question: After cigarette smoking, what is recognized as the second leading cause of lung cancer?

options.A: Radon gas exposure
options.B: Asbestos inhalation
options.C: Secondhand tobacco smoke
options.D: Airborne coal dust

explanation: Spot on! Radon is a natural radioactive gas that can build up in buildings. After smoking, it's the next big culprit behind lung cancer. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h2)

question: A psychiatric nurse visits a client at home and notices early signs of a psychiatric relapse. What action should the nurse take first?

options.A: Advise the family to immediately lock the client inside a room until the mood passes
options.B: Review the current treatment plan, assess stressors, and collaborate with the multidisciplinary team
options.C: Wait for the client to come to the distant tertiary hospital next year
options.D: Discharge the client from the CBR program because treatment has failed

explanation: Early intervention involves assessing what triggered the relapse, adjusting support, and working with the team before full hospitalization becomes necessary. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h3)

question: What is the medical term for the gradual loss of muscle mass and strength as people age?

options.A: Presbyopia
options.B: Sarcopenia
options.C: Osteoporosis
options.D: Atherosclerosis

explanation: Spot on! Sarcopenia is the natural, progressive shrinking of skeletal muscle that happens as we grow older. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T2#GNS321_U3_T2_h4)

question: According to the Frank-Starling law, what happens when more blood returns to the heart?

options.A: The ventricles stretch more and pump out a stronger stroke volume
options.B: Myocardial oxygen consumption decreases significantly
options.C: The intercalated discs close tightly to prevent over-expansion
options.D: The heart rate drops immediately to allow more filling time

explanation: Think of the heart like a rubber band: the more it stretches as it fills with blood, the stronger it snaps back to pump that blood out! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T10#GNS121_U3_T10_h6)

question: Which of these is most likely to make a community reject an IEC material?

options.A: It is handed out by a registered community health nurse.
options.B: It contains too many pictures and too little heavy medical jargon.
options.C: It is printed using black ink instead of colorful ink.
options.D: It violates local social norms or triggers cultural taboos.

explanation: Even if your medical facts are 100% correct, a community will quickly turn away from materials that clash with their cultural values or taboos. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h2)

question: When does the nurse's role in bereavement support typically begin?

options.A: Immediately after the patient's death and during the family's grieving process
options.B: Only after the funeral service has concluded
options.C: Months before the patient is admitted to the hospital
options.D: When the insurance company clears the final medical bill

explanation: Bereavement support starts right after death with post-mortem care and continues through follow-up outreach to help survivors cope with their loss. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T13#GNS321_U4_T13_h8)

question: Why must you always give thiamine BEFORE IV glucose to a malnourished patient?

options.A: Glucose lowers blood pressure too quickly without thiamine present
options.B: Thiamine makes the veins less fragile before a large fluid bolus is given
options.C: Glucose interacts with IV tubing and causes the medication to crystallize
options.D: Giving glucose first can use up remaining thiamine and worsen brain damage

question: Which of these is NOT a typical chronic condition that threatens an older adult's independence?

options.A: Mild seasonal allergies
options.B: Diabetic nerve damage
options.C: Heart failure
options.D: Stroke

explanation: That's right! While allergies can be annoying, they don't cause long-term disability like major strokes, heart issues, or nerve damage do. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T5#GNS324_U3_T5_h4)

question: In patient safety, what is a "near miss"?

options.A: A patient who successfully recovers from a major illness
options.B: An error that almost happened or was caught just before harming the patient
options.C: A medication that was prescribed but never manufactured
options.D: A nurse who arrived just seconds before her shift started

explanation: Wonderful! A near miss is a free warning sign that lets us fix problems before a real patient is hurt. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h5)

question: A nurse carefully documents every single dressing change and item used on a patient's chart. How does this affect hospital financing?

options.C: It guarantees the patient will be discharged the same day
options.D: It ensures accurate billing and prevents loss of facility revenue

explanation: Good documentation means the hospital accurately accounts for every service given, ensuring proper insurance reimbursement and keeping the clinic funded to help the next patient. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h7)

question: What is the outermost layer of the skin called?

options.A: Subcutaneous layer

options.C: Hypodermis

question: How can Nigeria best achieve long-term financial sustainability for its health care system?

options.A: By relying entirely on temporary grants from foreign philanthropic groups
options.B: By eliminating all user fees without replacing them with prepaid funds
options.C: By increasing domestic public funding and expanding mandatory health insurance
options.D: By closing all primary health care centers to focus on private clinics

explanation: Sustainable healthcare needs reliable local revenue through government budgets and risk-pooling mechanisms like health insurance. Brilliant work completing this set today! [learn more](GST322_U4_T3#GST322_U4_T3_h8)

question: Why should a nurse always wear gloves when applying a strong hormone cream to a patient's skin?

options.A: To keep the nurse's hands completely sterile during the procedure
options.B: To make sure the cream spreads more evenly across the patient's body
options.C: To prevent the nurse from absorbing the active drug through their own skin
options.D: To prevent the patient from feeling cold during the skin application

explanation: Topical medications can easily soak through your skin as you apply them. Wearing gloves protects you from accidentally absorbing active drugs into your own body! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h4)

question: A nurse is caring for an adult with diabetes who works on a farm. What is the most important health risk to keep an eye on?

options.A: Absence of any need for routine immunization boosters
options.B: Complete resistance to vector-borne diseases
options.C: Increased susceptibility to infections due to chronic illness
options.D: Immediate lifelong immunity acquired from farm work

question: What actually happens when there is 'sampling bias' in research?

options.A: An error caused by using a broken weighing scale in the clinic
options.B: The refusal of patients to answer personal questions in a survey
options.C: A systematic flaw that favors certain individuals over others in selection
options.D: The natural mathematical difference between a sample and a population

explanation: Spot on! Sampling bias means your selection method accidentally gives some people a better chance of being picked than others, skewing your results. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T18#GNS224_U1_T18_h6)

question: Which sign is a clinical indicator of severe respiratory distress in an adult patient?

options.A: Relaxed posture in a flat bed

question: What is a major ethical worry when using tele-nursing communication?

options.A: Preventing patients from buying medications at local pharmacies

options.C: Maintaining patient privacy and data confidentiality over digital networks
options.D: Eliminating the need to write nursing notes in patient files

explanation: Well reasoned! Sending health info over phones or the internet can expose it to unauthorized people, making data privacy a huge ethical duty for nurses. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T7#GNS113_U3_T7_h6)

question: What is the biggest plus of using a collaborating conflict style?

options.C: It avoids face-to-face conversation entirely
options.D: It requires very little time during a busy shift

question: An older patient complains that food tastes bland. Which age-related change causes this?

options.A: Hyper-sensitivity of the tongue nerves

options.C: Increased production of stomach acid
options.D: Decline in taste buds and olfactory nerve function

question: Which factor strongly influences a client's choice regarding contraceptive use?

question: A patient is scheduled for a surgical procedure on both legs requiring complete lower body numbness without general anesthesia. Which route of administration is the surgical team most likely to select?

question: How does taking time to build good rapport with a patient help your qualitative interview?

options.C: It makes the participant tell the researcher what they want to hear

question: What is the primary goal of harm reduction strategies in community nursing?

options.A: To minimize negative health and social consequences of drug use

options.D: To ignore drug use until the person asks for help

question: Why should digital health training be part of nursing education?

question: Which type of arthritis is most commonly caused by normal wear and tear on the joints over the years?

question: Which of these is a core part of a healthcare system?

question: Why do many follicles start growing at first, but usually only one reaches full maturity?

question: What safety check must you always perform before sending a patient for an MRI scan?

question: How is prevalence different from incidence?

options.D: Prevalence ignores people who are currently receiving care

question: What does a negative correlation mean between two variables?

question: An IV infusion of 1000 mL normal saline is ordered to run over 8 hours using an electronic pump. What is the rate in mL/hr?

question: Which medication is the main choice for treating onchocerciasis?

question: Why do care teams use psychiatric parole instead of keeping a stable patient locked away long-term?

question: What is the primary focus of health maintenance?

question: Why is it important for a nurse manager to understand their hospital's chain of command?

options.C: To avoid having to communicate with any physicians or doctors

question: What is the main thing that sets a medical emergency apart from a trauma case?

options.C: It develops slowly over several months without sudden changes

question: Why should nurses avoid using judgmental words in patient notes (like 'uncooperative' or 'difficult')?

question: You just received a new supply of liquid pentavalent vaccines for your clinic fridge. Where should you place them?

question: How does Psychological First Aid differ from traditional psychotherapy?

options.B: PFA requires a licensed psychiatrist to perform it

question: What happens to dissolved oxygen in a body of water when raw sewage creates a high biochemical oxygen demand (BOD)?

options.C: Oxygen turns directly into toxic chlorine gas bubbles
options.D: Oxygen levels rise rapidly, causing plants to grow too fast

question: Why is herd immunity so helpful for vulnerable people in a community?

options.A: It guarantees that every single person in the population will develop permanent natural immunity

options.D: It reduces overall disease spread, indirectly protecting those who cannot be vaccinated

question: A patient is prescribed a new synergistic drug combo. What is a key nursing duty before giving it?

question: Why is it important for a community nurse to respect local cultural beliefs when planning health programs?

options.C: It is a legal requirement for writing a hospital admission note

question: Why do people with early cataracts often complain about blinding glare when driving at night?

question: During triage, a patient has severe head injuries, no pulse, and is not breathing even after opening the airway. What START category do they get?

question: What is the main characteristic of a cross-sectional descriptive study?

question: How much water should a nurse use to flush a gastrostomy tube between different medications?

options.C: 1 to 2 mL of sterile saline

question: How should a nurse document anatomical findings related to FGM in a patient's chart?

question: Why must a researcher use a retrospective study rather than a live experiment when studying the health effects of a toxic chemical spill?

question: Why is organizing raw patient data important in nursing informatics?

question: Which type of FGM involves removing the clitoris along with part or all of the labia minora?

question: Which healthcare professional frequently acts as the central coordinator within a multidisciplinary care team for chronic degenerative conditions?

question: Which communication tool remains especially reliable for reaching remote areas during electrical power failures?

question: How do common respiratory germs usually leave an infected person's body?
